text:
anika: opened PR to refresh Cetus-11B model card + migration notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4388. Goals: move bench assets into repo, normalize display name vs runtime alias, fix a broken assets link, and update SDK snippet to async v4 with a streaming example.

bryce: saw the preview. one of the bench CSV links points at s3://storage.redwood.ai/bench/cetus/throughput.csv which got deleted last week. infra prefers bench CSVs to live under docs/assets/bench/cetus.

link-bot: linkcheck: 2 broken links found (docs/model-sources.md#L5, s3://storage.redwood.ai/bench/cetus/throughput.csv). Recommendation: copy bench CSV into docs/assets/bench/cetus and remove absolute storage URLs from docs pages; replace with provenance note.

taylor: also the card mixes 'Cetus-11B' and 'cetus11b' in examples. runtime aliasing resolves but customers get confused during pinning. add an "aliases" line and a YAML pin example showing both display and alias forms.

morgan: SDK note: current snippet uses the old sync client and assumes resp['text']. new v4 async response shape is resp['choices'][0]['message']['content']. i'll add both a simple async example and a streaming example.

anika: sample async snippet I'll include: ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
resp = await client.generate(model="cetus-11b", prompt="Summarize logs")
print(resp['choices'][0]['message']['content'])
```

bryce: for streaming please show how to handle partial chunks. small example suggestion: ```python
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()
async for chunk in client.generate_stream(model="cetus-11b", prompt="Draft a release note"):
    # chunk is a dict fragment; append to buffer or render live
    print(chunk.get('delta', ''), end='')
```

taylor: migration YAML pin example request: show hyphen vs alias: ```yaml
routes:
  - model: Cetus-11B
    aliases: [cetus11b, cetus-11b-int8]
    pinned_variant: cetus11b-int8
```

anika: good. i'll add a short "provenance" paragraph linking upstream model page + license and remove direct weight/download URLs from model-sources.md.

link-bot: deploy-preview built. linkcheck now reports 1 broken link: s3://storage.redwood.ai/models/cetus/weights.tar.gz still referenced from docs/model-sources.md.

bryce: i'll copy throughput.csv into docs/assets/bench/cetus and update the card to reference the local asset (ETA today EOD). anyone want to proofread the measurement methodology wording?

morgan: i'll add the measurement methodology subsection: seq_len=2048, batch=4, batch_window=150ms, hardware=4xA100-40G. include the exact runner args so numbers are reproducible. also clarify table units: "tokens/sec" and indicate whether it's aggregate or per-GPU.

taylor: tiny nit: clarify whether numbers include KV-cache warmup. add a footnote if not.

anika: done—added methodology + KV-cache note and a small footnote about quant-fallback differences.

bryce: pushed the throughput.csv into docs/assets/bench/cetus and flipped the links. CI running.

ci-bot: CI: linkcheck failed (1): s3://storage.redwood.ai/models/cetus/weights.tar.gz referenced in docs/model-sources.md. Please remove or replace.

anika: removed the storage URL from model-sources.md and pointed readers at the provenance block in the model card. pushed.

ci-bot: CI passed. linkcheck clean. preview URL: https://deployments.preview.redwood.ai/docs/cetus-11b-card

anika: merging after green. thanks for the quick reviews. will open a follow-up to add streaming error-handling patterns to the SDK guide. :rocket:
